title: Long UAL — Formal Versailles Ceasefire Unlocks Fuel Relief + Middle East Route Recovery
entry: Enter $115–122 (UAL at $118.80 June 17 close, pulled back from $124.79 ATH June 15 on the FOMC hawkish shock). The formal Versailles digital signing by Trump and Pezeshkian June 17 plus Pakistan's June 18 Hormuz confirmation is categorically stronger than the June 14 Islamabad Declaration that drove the first ATH — this is a signed deal with immediate implementation, not a framework. Scale: 70% at $117–120 on June 18 open; 30% add if UAL dips to $115–117 on intraday FOMC macro noise. Do NOT chase above $124.
stop_loss: $108 daily close (~9% below $119 entry midpoint) — implies Iran ceasefire implementation fails within 10 days (Hormuz mine-clearance blocked by IRGC or a rogue mine detonation near a US vessel restarts escalation), driving Brent back above $88 on two consecutive sessions and restoring the fuel-cost headwind that suppressed UAL through the April–June conflict period
targets: $128 — reclaims the pre-FOMC ceasefire ATH zone; June Q2 management commentary confirms fuel cost savings are visible in unit cost guidance; Iran deal implementation proceeding on schedule; +7.6% from $119 midpoint

$142 — H2 2026 capacity restoration: UAL re-opens key Middle East routes (Istanbul, Dubai, Amman) with WTI at $72–75 structurally confirmed below $80; Q2 earnings late July show fuel expense 18–22% lower YoY; $142 is the pre-conflict-escalation analyst consensus range; +19.3%

$158 — full oil-normalization upside: sustained WTI $68–72 through H2; international load factors recover as Middle East travel resumes; UAL FY2026 EPS estimate upgrades of 25–30% flow through on fuel savings plus demand recovery; approaches prior 52-week high zone; +32.8%
catalyst: The Trump–Pezeshkian digital ceasefire signing at the Palace of Versailles on June 17, 2026, and Pakistan's June 18 confirmation that the Strait of Hormuz reopens immediately, is a categorically different event from the June 14 Islamabad Declaration (unsigned, contested by Iranian domestic factions). UAL reached an ATH of $124.79 on June 15 when the initial framework emerged, then pulled back to $118.80 on June 17 as the FOMC hawkish shock (9 hike dots, 3.8% median, Warsh dropping forward guidance) compressed all equity multiples. The oil-cost thesis is now reinforced by formal implementation: WTI at $74.82 on June 18 is the sixth consecutive lower session, and Iranian supply of up to 1.5 million bpd begins re-entering the market within 60 days per Pakistan's confirmation.
thesis:
United Airlines is the highest-operating-leverage beneficiary of the WTI price correction in the S&P 500. Jet fuel represents approximately 23–27% of UAL's total operating cost. During the April–June 2026 Iran conflict, WTI averaged $85–93 per barrel — a $10–18 premium above the pre-conflict $75 level. At UAL's fuel consumption of approximately 3.8 billion gallons annually, each $10 decline in jet fuel prices translates to roughly $1.0–1.1 billion in annualized cost savings. WTI at $74.82 on June 18 versus the ~$90 conflict-period average is a $1.5–1.7 billion annual tailwind that sell-side analysts have not yet incorporated into H2 2026 EPS estimates. The earnings estimate upgrade cycle — lagging the oil price move by 3–5 weeks — is the medium-term stock catalyst.

The pullback from $124.79 ATH to $118.80 was purely macro-driven (FOMC hawkish shock) rather than any deterioration in the oil thesis. The formal Versailles signing on June 17 and Pakistan's June 18 Hormuz confirmation actually strengthens the setup relative to June 15: the deal is now signed and implementation has begun, removing the 'framework vs. signed deal' uncertainty that capped the first rally. The $6 pullback into the $115–122 entry zone is the intended entry that the prior ceasefire framework-driven ATH denied — the FOMC shock inadvertently created the entry.

Middle East route revenue is the second-leg catalyst. UAL serves Dubai, Doha, Istanbul, and Amman as key international hubs. Flights to and from Gulf Cooperation Council countries were disrupted during April–June — both due to airspace restrictions and demand suppression. With the ceasefire and Hormuz reopening, international travel demand to and through the Middle East begins recovering in a 30–60 day window. UAL's international revenue per available seat mile is approximately 15% higher than domestic RASM; a Middle East recovery adds a revenue kicker above and beyond the fuel cost savings.

The counter-party is the airline bear who argues: (1) Hormuz mine-clearance takes 2–4 weeks minimum — any delay or Iranian domestic political complication sends oil back above $80; (2) FOMC hawkishness compresses consumer discretionary spending, reducing leisure travel demand that props domestic fares; (3) UAL has already rallied 66% from its 52-week low of $71.55, so the easy money is made. The $108 stop at 9% below entry captures all three risks without creating outsized loss if any materialize.
bull_case: Hormuz mine-clearance proceeds ahead of schedule (US Navy mine-clearing vessels pre-positioned since the Islamabad Declaration); Iranian crude visible on AIS tracking by June 25. UAL gaps to $122–124 on June 18; June 22 gap-up continues if three-way BUY condition met. Q2 guidance revision at the July 22 earnings call shows fuel cost per gallon at $2.65 vs. $3.10 in the conflict peak. UAL to $142 (Target 2) by late July.
bear_case: Iranian hardliners (IRGC) block Hormuz mine-clearance — a rogue mine detonation near a US vessel on June 20–22 restarts escalation. Brent spikes from $78 back to $87 in a single session. UAL gaps down from $118 toward $108–110 on Monday June 22. FOMC hawkish follow-through compresses travel demand and airline earnings multiples. Stop at $108 triggered on the first daily close below that level.
invalidation: $108 daily close; OR Brent closes above $88 on two consecutive sessions (deal implementation collapse signal); OR UAL Q2 guidance update shows fuel cost savings below 8% YoY (estimates not moving as expected); OR VIX spikes above 25 (recession fear dominates ceasefire benefit)
